abstract: This is a phase 1b/2 study of a single dose of intravenous (IV) bacteriophage in males and non-pregnant females, at least 18 years old, diagnosed with Cystic Fibrosis (CF). This clinical trial is designed to assess the safety and microbiological activity of bacteriophage product Walter Reed Army Institute of Research- PAM-Cystic Fibrosis1 (WRAIR-PAM-CF1), directed at Pseudomonas aeruginosa in clinically stable CF individuals chronically colonized with P. aeruginosa. WRAIR-PAM-CF1 is a 4 component anti-pseudomonal bacteriophage mixture containing between 4 x 10\^7 and 4 x 10\^9 Plaque Forming Units (PFU) of bacteriophage. Enrollment will occur at up to 20 clinical sites in the United States. In stage 1, two eligible subjects will be assigned to each of the three dosing arms receiving a single dosage of the IV bacteriophage therapy (4 x 10\^7 PFU, 4 x 10\^8 PFU, and 4 x 10\^9 PFU; total of 6 sentinel subjects), followed by 30 plus or minus 7 days observation period. If no Serious Adverse Events (SAEs)(related to the study product) are identified during the 96 hours after bacteriophage administration for all Sentinel Subjects in Stage 1, the study will proceed to Stage 2. In Stage 2a, 32 subjects will be enrolled into one of 4 arms (placebo IV, 4 x 10\^7 PFU, 4 x 10\^8 PFU, and 4 x 10\^9 PFU) in a 1:1:1:1 allocation. An interim analysis will be performed after all subjects have completed follow up visit 5 on Day 8+3 to select the IV bacteriophage dose with the most favorable safety and microbiological activity profile. During Stage 2b, subjects will be randomized into the bacteriophage (dose selected based on Interim Analysis following Stage 2a) or placebo arm. The final sample size is expected to be up to 72 subjects total with up to 25 subjects in the placebo arm and up to 25 subjects in the Stage 2b bacteriophage dose.

abstract: In crab aquaculture, carotenoids exert indispensable and multifaceted functions that extend well beyond pigmentation, influencing hepatopancreas and ovary development. As crabs cannot synthesize carotenoids de novo, these compounds must be supplied through the diet. This review summarizes current knowledge of the physiological significance, metabolic pathways and functional mechanisms of carotenoids in crabs. It also examines the complex processes of carotenoid absorption, transport, tissue-specific deposition and enzymatic transformations, including cleavage and isomerization, while highlighting the significant gaps that remain in our understanding of the regulatory networks governing these processes. This review is expected to deepen the recognition of carotenoids as multifunctional health factors, to promote the use of synthetic biology and metabolic engineering in the development of microbial platforms for high-value carotenoids such as astaxanthin, and to formulate precise dietary strategies that improve crab cultures.

abstract: Black spot shell syndrome is a polymicrobial shell disease of crustaceans that can impair host fitness and reduce fishery value, yet it has not previously been documented in the marble crab, Metacarcinus edwardsii, in Chile. This study characterised the prevalence of black spot shell syndrome and the associated culturable bacterial assemblage in M. edwardsii from northern Chilean Patagonia. In August 2023, 2518 crabs were sampled across three fishing grounds in the Aysén Region and examined for lesion presence, lesion coverage and host traits, while bacteria from unaffected and affected carapaces were cultured and identified by 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Overall prevalence was 13.7%; occurrence differed among sites, increased with carapace width and was not associated with sex. Among affected crabs, lesion coverage also varied among sites and showed no association with sex or carapace width. Forty-three bacterial isolates representing seven genera were recovered, with members of the Pseudomonas fluorescens species complex predominating across lesion stages. Several Pseudomonas isolates exhibited chitinolytic and proteolytic activities consistent with a potential role in cuticle degradation. However, these findings do not establish Pseudomonas as the primary aetiological agent of the syndrome. These findings provide the first epidemiological and microbiological baseline evidence of black spot shell syndrome in M. edwardsii in Chile and highlight the need for continued surveillance, culture-independent microbiome profiling and targeted pathogenicity studies.

abstract: The global rise in invasive fungal infections and antifungal resistance highlights an urgent need for new antifungal scaffolds. Using a focused phenotypic screening approach in yeast, we identified the leelamine isonitrile GB-79 as a potent inhibitor of fungal growth. The compound displayed potent antifungal activity in vitro across genetically diverse strains, with lower IC50 values than fluconazole under the experimental conditions tested. Importantly, GB-79 showed strong activity against clinical isolates of Candida albicans, Candida parapsilosis, and Nakaseomyces glabratus (formerly known as Candida glabrata), including strains with reduced susceptibility to existing antifungal agents. In vivo, GB-79 was well tolerated in mice following single-dose oral administration at doses up to 100 mg/kg, with no mortality or marked body-weight changes. Despite high systemic clearance, low exposure after intravenous dosing, and poor oral bioavailability, GB-79 reduced renal fungal burden in C. albicans-infected animals. These findings establish GB-79 as a promising antifungal scaffold and demonstrate the value of phenotypic screening strategies for uncovering new chemical entities with translational potential. GB-79 provides a promising foundation for medicinal chemistry optimization and further development of next-generation antifungal therapeutics.

abstract: BACKGROUND: Necrotising soft tissue infections (NSTIs) are rapidly progressive infections requiring prompt diagnosis and management. This study assessed predictors of mortality, microbiological spectrum, antimicrobial resistance patterns, and differences between polymicrobial and monomicrobial NSTIs in a prospective manner. METHODS: This study enrolled patients aged 15 years or older with clinically suspected NSTIs who presented between March 2022 and February 2023. Clinical, laboratory, surgical, and outcome data were collected. Tissue and pus samples were processed for aerobic and anaerobic cultures. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed according to CLSI guidelines. Mortality-associated factors were analysed using univariate analysis, binary logistic regression, and survival analysis. RESULTS: Eighty-seven patients were included, predominantly male (87.3%), with a median age of 47.5 years. Extremities were most commonly affected. The mortality rate of this cohort was 25.3%. Polymicrobial infections predominated (49.4%), while monomicrobial NSTIs were associated with higher mortality (p = 0.022). Gram-negative organisms, particularly Acinetobacter baumannii and Escherichia coli, were the most frequent pathogens. Obligate anaerobes were significantly associated with polymicrobial infections. Chronic liver disease (p = 0.003) and systemic toxicity (p = 0.018) independently predicted mortality, whereas higher haemoglobin levels were protective. High antimicrobial resistance was observed, including carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii and Enterobacterales. Among the anaerobes, resistance to clindamycin and cefoxitin, along with reduced susceptibility to metronidazole, was reported. CONCLUSION: NSTIs remain associated with substantial mortality, especially in monomicrobial infections due to multidrug-resistant Gram-negative pathogens. Early recognition, prompt surgery, and region-specific empirical antimicrobial therapy are crucial for improving outcomes.

abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is a major public health issue. Methicillin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is one of the indicators that is monitored particularly closely. In animals, pig farms, among others, have been identified as reservoirs of MRSA, with a risk of transmission to humans, particularly to individuals in direct contact with livestock. In France, the prevalence of MRSA in pig farms has increased markedly in recent years. While cross-species transmission between pigs and humans in professional settings is well-documented, the temporal dynamics, the actual incidence of acquisition, and the associated determinants remain insufficiently characterized in France. Adopting a "One Health" approach, this project aims to gain a better understanding of the mechanisms by which MRSA spreads between animal and human subpopulations and to incorporate these insights into a mathematical modeling framework.

Susceptibility profiles were determined by broth microdilution and genomes sequenced with Oxford Nanopore. RESULTS: All isolates produced carbapenemases: 48% KPC, 20% NDM, 4.4% VIM, 27.6% multi-carbapenemase producers. Resistance to carbapenems, fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, and co-trimoxazole exceeded 90%, except for amikacin (73.4%) and colistin (46.5%). Aztreonam-avibactam and cefepime-zidebactam showed the highest susceptibility, 94.5% and 91.6% respectively, yet resistance was >10% among multi-carbapenemase producers. High levels of resistance to cefiderocol (41.7%) and cefepime-taniborbactam (21.4%) were detected. Aztreonam-avibactam resistance co-occurred with VEB-25 and a novel VEB variant. Predominant sequence types included ST39 (28.1%), ST11 (22.7%), and ST258 (18.4%). Time-scaled phylogenies demonstrated that following CG importation CR-Kp often acquired multiple carbapenemases. Over 88% of isolates were implicated in transmission clusters involving 1-8 ICUs across the country. CONCLUSIONS: In Greek ICUs, CR-Kp appears to emerge via local plasmid acquisition and then spread within and between hospitals. While aztreonam-avibactam and cefepime-zidebactam remain promising treatment options, resistance among multi-carbapenemase producers and diagnostic gaps (notably for VEB variants) are concerning.

This study compares the efficacy of continuous infusion (CI) versus conventional intermittent dosing (ID) of CZA in critically ill ICU patients with severe infections caused by K. pneumoniae OXA-48 or P. aeruginosa. One hundred forty critically ill ICU patients requiring CZA treatment will be randomized to receive either ID (2 g/0.5 g every 8 hours over 2 hours) or an equivalent dose in CI (6 g/1.5 g continuously over 24 hours). The primary outcome is the microbiological success rate. Secondary outcomes include clinical success rate, time to symptom improvement, length of ICU and hospital stay, 28-day all-cause mortality, pathogen recurrence rate, time to weaning from mechanical ventilation, cumulative vasoactive-inotropic score, adverse events, and the ratio of ceftazidime plasma concentration to the pathogen's minimum inhibitory concentration (C/MIC). This trial seeks to provide evidence on the optimal administration strategy for CZA in critically ill ICU patients with severe infections due to MDR G- pathogens.

abstract: Transcriptomic approaches are widely used to study the stress biology of fungi or other (micro)organisms. When three or more transcriptomes are compared, considering their relative positions can clarify their relations. Here we represent transcriptomes as points in an N-dimensional space (transcriptome space), where dimensions measure the transcriptional intensities of genes. In this space stress responses correspond to vectors from the pretreatment transcriptome to the transcriptome altered by the treatment. This approach enables us to create simple definitions that let us focus on the data measured in the experiment. In addition, we show (1) the importance of kinetic studies in comparing stress responses, especially when examining responses to changes of different magnitudes; (2) how a reference transcriptome with genes expressed near the upper and lower ends of their transcriptional range constrains stress responses; (3) why the pre-treatment difference between transcriptomes makes the evaluation process difficult. We also show that comprehending the results of combinatorial stress response experiments is disproportionately challenging because of the cumulative nature of the problems mentioned above in these experiments. We propose that considering the relations of transcriptomes as points in the transcriptome space provides a view that complements the standard gene-centered analyses. Developing a model that describes the processes resulting in the observed relative position of transcriptomes can help reduce the risk of misinterpreting transcriptional changes at the level of individual genes or gene groups.

abstract: Antifungal resistance in Candida species has become a critical yet underrecognized public health challenge. While most efforts focus on hospital transmission and clinical antifungal use, growing evidence implicates environmental, animal-associated, and community niches in the emergence and spread of resistant Candida. Agricultural practices, ecosystem pollution, and wastewater contamination create selective conditions that can favor resistance beyond clinical exposure, while climate pressures reshape fungal adaptation and spread. Addressing upstream ecological drivers is essential to contain the expanding threat of antifungal-resistant Candida and safeguard the effectiveness of current and future treatments.

abstract: RATIONALE: Cavitary lung cancer, particularly squamous cell carcinoma (SCC), can closely mimic infectious cavitary diseases such as pulmonary aspergillosis. When molecular pathogen testing yields a positive result, the infectious diagnosis may be erroneously reinforced, and histological confirmation may be delayed. PATIENT CONCERNS: A 68-year-old male farmer with a 40 pack-year smoking history presented with a 6-month history of cough, expectoration, and chest tightness. Chest computed tomography revealed a 66 mm × 70 mm thick-walled cavitary lesion in the left upper lobe. Targeted next-generation sequencing of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid at the referring hospital detected Aspergillus flavus sequences, leading to a misdiagnosis of pulmonary aspergillosis and 2.5 months of voriconazole therapy, during which the lesion progressed. DIAGNOSES: Repeat bronchoscopy at our institution revealed a fistulous opening with intracavitary nodules and necrotic material. Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration (EBUS-TBNA) at stations 4 L and 10 L confirmed poorly differentiated lung SCC. 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET-CT) demonstrated hypermetabolism in the primary lesion, mediastinal lymph nodes, and sternum, supporting a clinical-radiological diagnosis of stage IVA (cT4N2M1b) disease. INTERVENTIONS: The patient received first-line paclitaxel plus carboplatin combined with tislelizumab for 6 cycles, followed by tislelizumab maintenance monotherapy. OUTCOMES: A partial response according to the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1 was achieved after the first cycle, with sustained tumor shrinkage after 6 cycles and no evidence of disease progression during ongoing maintenance therapy. LESSONS: In cavitary lung lesions, targeted next-generation sequencing detection of fungal sequences should not by itself override the need for histological evaluation, because molecular assays cannot distinguish colonization or contamination from invasive infection. Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration combined with positron emission tomography/computed tomography is valuable for diagnosis and staging when cavitary malignancy is suspected, and SCC remains an important subtype of cavitary lung cancer in long-term smokers.

Patients with cystic fibrosis frequently manifest fungal sensitization and fungal colonization with Aspergillus fumigatus.6 Aspergillus species also has a cause-and-effect relationship with non-CF (cystic fibrosis) bronchiectasis.7, 8 In allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA), Aspergillus is the cause of bronchiectasis. In contrast, in other causes of bronchiectasis, A fumigatus can theoretically promote allergic response, which may result in poor lung function, increase the risk of exacerbations, and even cause ABPA over time.9, 10 In a recent study, we found an overall prevalence of Aspergillus sensitization of 29.5% and the prevalence of chronic aspergillus infection was 76%.11 The prevalence of chronic aspergillus colonization in non-(tuberculosis) TB-non-CF fibrosis was 47.5% (49/103).11 By mechanism similar to chronic bacterial colonization, chronic aspergillus infection or aspergillus sensitization can increase the risk of bronchiectasis exacerbation. Therefore, eradication of A. fumigatus from the airways of patients with bronchiectasis would decrease the future risk of a bronchiectasis exacerbation. Notably, in ABPA, use of itraconazole and voriconazole reduce the exacerbations by reducing the fungal burden in the airways.12, 13 In this randomized trial, we will investigate whether treatment with oral itraconazole for six months would reduce the future risk of bronchiectasis exacerbation in patients with non-CF-non-ABPA bronchiectasis.

abstract: Patients with leukemia are treated with intensive chemotherapy and often have to undergo a stem cell transplantation which makes their immune system extremely vulnerable. This puts them at risk for invasive fungal infections, of which invasive mucormycosis (IM) is one of the most dangerous ones. Treatment of IM is complex and mortality rates are still extremely high, ranging from 40% to 80% and sometimes even higher if the central nervous system is involved. Mucormycosis requires immediate intervention due to the rapidly progressive and destructive nature of the infection. But the diagnosis is often made too late… Better survival can be achieved with a faster diagnosis. A new test has recently been developed for detection of Mucorales DNA by PCR. The polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is a method that allows to quickly make millions of copies of, for example, Mucorales DNA in order to detect it in the blood at an early stage. Because blood can easily be obtained, without an additional burden on the patient, the test could be interesting for screening for these infections, which then offers the opportunity to start an adequate treatment more quickly. However, the test is now only performed if there is a clinical suspicion of IM. But at that point, precious time has already been lost, and often the patient can no longer be cured. In this study the utility of the Mucorales PCR as a possible screening test in at-risk patients is assessed. The participants, hospitalised patients with leukemia, will be screened twice weekly with a Mucorales PCR test during their most vulnerable period. If the study shows that the test helps in diagnosing IM faster, this could have an important impact on the treatment and survival of these at-risk patients.

abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the clinical efficacy, safety and operational feasibility of a low-dose regional citrate anticoagulation (RCA) combined with low-dose nafamostat mesylate (NM) mixed anticoagulation regimen in continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) for patients with liver failure, so as to provide clinical reference for the selection of CRRT anticoagulation strategies for such special high-risk critically ill patients. METHOD: A retrospective case series study was conducted. Eleven patients with liver failure who received CRRT in the Department of Critical Care Medicine, Zhongnan Hospital of Wuhan University were enrolled. All patients were treated with CVVHDF mode and uniformly implemented the low-dose citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation regimen. CRRT treatment parameters, anticoagulant drugs, and infusion doses of calcium and sodium bicarbonate were standardized. The monitoring frequency of peripheral blood gas and activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) and the criteria for dose stratification adjustment were standardized. Data including patients' demographic baseline data, CRRT treatment duration, filter service life, blood gas electrolytes, dynamic changes of APTT, pipeline and filter coagulation, bleeding and metabolic adverse events, organ function and clinical outcomes were collected for summary and analysis. RESULTS: A total of 11 patients with liver failure undergoing CRRT in CVVHDF mode were enrolled in this study, using the low-dose regional citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation regimen. After treatment, the median filter life of patients reached 48 (38, 68.75) hours, with no severe pipeline or filter coagulation; there were no significant abnormalities in systemic coagulation indicators. One case (9.1%) had mild oral mucosal bleeding; no severe massive bleeding occurred. Hypocalcemia and metabolic alkalosis were observed in several patients but were not severe, and no citrate accumulation, severe hypocalcemia, or severe acid-base or electrolyte disorders occurred. PCT was lower than baseline (P = 0.005) and APACHE II score was improved (P = 0.011) over the course of ICU treatment; however, all patients simultaneously received antibiotics, vasopressors, source control, and other ICU supportive care, and these changes therefore cannot be attributed to the mixed anticoagulation regimen. Liver and kidney function showed no obvious deterioration. CONCLUSION: In this small, single-center retrospective case series, a low-dose regional citrate combined with nafamostat mixed anticoagulation regimen was feasible to implement in patients with liver failure receiving CRRT. In this cohort, the median filter life was 48 h, no severe filter or pipeline coagulation was observed, and no citrate accumulation, severe hypocalcemia, or severe acid-base or electrolyte disorders occurred; one case (9.1%) had mild bleeding. Because no comparator group was included, whether these observations reflect a benefit of the mixed regimen over conventional RCA, nafamostat alone, systemic heparin, or no anticoagulation cannot be determined. These findings are preliminary and hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in adequately powered, multicenter, prospective controlled trials.

abstract: BACKGROUND: Intensive care units (ICUs) are at high risk for healthcare-associated infections caused by Gram-negative carbapenem-resistant organisms (GN-CROs). Timely recognition of unusual resistance patterns and potential transmission clusters can be challenging where resources are limited. This study aimed to use electronic health record (EHR)-based surveillance to detect and characterize temporal and spatial clustering of GN-CROs in an adult ICU. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study using microbiological and clinical data from ICU patients admitted between January 2023 and December 2024. Positive cultures for GN-CROs were included. Potential clusters were initially defined as two or more isolates of the same species with identical resistance profiles identified in different patients within 20 days. We extracted data from the EHR and managed it in Research Electronic Data Capture. Temporal trends were assessed using Shewhart control charts, statistical exceedance was evaluated using Poisson probability thresholds, and spatial clustering was examined based on bed locations. Analyses were performed using R statistical software (Vanderbilt University, Nashville, Tennessee, USA) (version ≥4.0). RESULTS: Of 353 Gram-negative organisms isolated, 18% (63/353) were carbapenem resistant. CONCLUSIONS: EHR-based surveillance identified epidemiologically meaningful clusters, triggering transmission investigations. Integrating temporal, spatial, and statistical methods offers a feasible approach for outbreak triggers where molecular typing is unavailable.

abstract: Drug dosing during continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is difficult in critically ill patients because drug exposure is influenced by both the patient and the extracorporeal treatment. This narrative review provides a practical overview of drug dosing during CRRT, while intermittent hemodialysis and sustained low-efficiency dialysis are discussed only where they provide relevant contextual or comparative information. It summarizes the main drug-related, patient-related, and treatment-related factors that influence extracorporeal drug clearance and discusses their clinical implications for commonly used drug classes. Loading and maintenance doses should be considered separately: loading doses depend mainly on volume of distribution and the need for early therapeutic exposure, whereas maintenance dosing depends on total clearance, including residual renal, extracorporeal, and non-renal clearance. Therapeutic drug monitoring can help guide dose adjustment when validated targets are available, while model-informed precision dosing may provide additional support in selected patients. The review also proposes an eight-step practical framework based on residual kidney function, the actual delivered CRRT prescription, drug pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, therapeutic monitoring, and repeated reassessment. Future approaches may combine real-time CRRT data with pharmacokinetic models to support more individualized dosing.

abstract: BACKGROUND: Invasive fungal pneumonia remains a diagnostic challenge in immunocompromised children with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), as conventional microbiological tests have limited sensitivity. This retrospective study evaluated whether serial chest computed tomography (CT) scored with the Radiologic Severity Index (RSI) was associated with initiation of antifungal therapy in 87 children with ALL and chemotherapy-related pneumonia. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 87 pediatric patients [median age 6.2 years, interquartile range (IQR) 3.5-8.0 years] diagnosed with ALL who developed pneumonia during chemotherapy between March 2016 and October 2024. Demographic data, medical history, and laboratory findings were collected for each patient. Chest CT images were assessed using the RSI, which quantifies affected lung volume and regional opacity (range 0-48). Clinical and radiologic characteristics of fungal and non-fungal pneumonia cases were compared using t-tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, Pearson's Chi-squared tests, or Fisher's exact tests. Additionally, binary logistic regression models were employed to examine the correlation between RSI and antifungal therapy initiation. RESULTS: No significant differences in baseline or peak RSI were observed between fungal and non-fungal groups, nor between antifungal-treated and untreated groups (all P>0.05). Routine laboratory parameters, including leukocyte, neutrophil, and lymphocyte counts, as well as serum albumin levels, did not differ between groups (all P>0.05). However, the antifungal-treated group demonstrated significantly higher change from baseline to peak Radiologic Severity Index (ΔRSI) (P=0.01) and RSI variation rate (P=0.02) compared to the untreated group. In multivariable logistic regression adjusted for potential confounders, neither ΔRSI [odds ratio (OR) =1.14, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.94-1.37, P=0.18] nor RSI variation rate (OR =0.54, 95% CI: 0.15-1.98, P=0.36) emerged as an independent predictor of antifungal therapy initiation. CONCLUSIONS: Dynamic RSI metrics (ΔRSI and RSI variation rate) are significantly elevated in pediatric ALL patients with chemotherapy-related pneumonia who receive antifungal therapy, whereas static RSI metrics and routine laboratory parameters are not. However, after adjusting for clinical confounders, dynamic RSI metrics do not independently predict antifungal treatment initiation. These findings suggest that serial CT monitoring and dynamic RSI assessment may reflect clinically meaningful disease progression, but current evidence does not support their use as standalone predictive tools for antifungal therapy decisions. Prospective studies with standardized imaging protocols are warranted to validate these exploratory results.

abstract: Nasopharyngeal mucormycosis is exceptionally rare, with only three prior cases reported. We describe a 19-year-old male without prior medical illness who presented with progressive left ear pain that was initially managed as external otitis. Three weeks later, he developed diabetic ketoacidosis from newly diagnosed diabetes mellitus. During hospitalization, bilateral complete facial nerve paralysis (House-Brackmann grade 6) developed on consecutive days. Computed tomography showed only nasopharyngeal mucosal thickening, but direct nasopharyngoscopy revealed a necrotic mass. Histopathology confirmed acute invasive mucormycosis. The patient received liposomal amphotericin B for one month, underwent endoscopic debridement, and was discharged on oral posaconazole for two months. The fungal infection resolved completely, but the bilateral facial palsy showed no improvement. This case represents the fourth reported instance of nasopharyngeal mucormycosis and the first in a previously healthy young adult presenting with bilateral complete facial nerve palsy. The clinical course emphasizes that new-onset diabetic ketoacidosis alone can create sufficient susceptibility for invasive mucormycosis even in immunocompetent individuals. Furthermore, severe cranial neuropathy may precede any typical radiographic findings, making prompt endoscopic evaluation and empirical antifungal therapy critical. Despite successful infection eradication, neurological deficits can persist as permanent sequelae.

abstract: Multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs) cause serious infections that are difficult to treat, leading to increased morbidity and mortality, longer hospital stays, and increased healthcare costs. Many risk factors for MDRO infections are present in the Veteran population (such as older age, underlying medical conditions like diabetes, and stays in long-term healthcare settings). Some people can carry these organisms in their gut. Even without current symptoms, carrying these MDROs also increases risk of future infection. Effective, easy to use, and inexpensive interventions to reduce gut carriage of MDROs are needed to reduce risk of infection. abstract: BACKGROUND: Carotid endarterectomy (CEA) is an established treatment for carotid artery stenosis. However, complex carotid bifurcation disease involving the proximal external carotid artery (ECA) may increase the technical difficulty of conventional CEA. Preoperative computed tomography angiography showed severe stenosis at the origin of the right internal carotid artery with concomitant proximal ECA involvement. CONCLUSIONS: The Crab technique may represent a technically feasible modification of conventional CEA in selected patients with complex carotid bifurcation disease involving the proximal ECA. However, its safety, durability, and appropriate indications require further evaluation in larger case series with longer imaging follow-up.

abstract: OBJECTIVES: To develop consensus-based, pragmatic recommendations for the diagnosis and management of fungal pneumonia in non-neutropenic critically ill adults in India and Asia, where the dual burden of mucormycosis and resource-limited healthcare settings creates distinct challenges. METHODS: Using a modified Delphi process, 20 multidisciplinary experts participated in the first round, and 19 completed the second and third rounds of anonymous voting on risk factors, diagnostic strategies, and management of invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA), pulmonary mucormycosis (PM), and Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP). Consensus was defined as ≥ 70% agreement or disagreement; statements with 60-69% agreement were categorized as "suggest," while the remaining were classified as "no consensus." RESULTS: Key risk factors included severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, influenza, COVID-19, diabetes mellitus, and chronic liver or kidney disease. A multimodal diagnostic strategy combining contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT), early bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL), microscopy, culture, and galactomannan (BAL threshold ≥ 1.0) was recommended, with molecular methods used where available. Liposomal amphotericin B was the preferred empiric agent in regions with high mucormycosis prevalence; voriconazole, posaconazole, or isavuconazole are first-line for proven IPA. Therapeutic drug monitoring is essential for azole antifungals, with a minimum treatment duration of 6-12 weeks. For PCP, empiric trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole is recommended in immunosuppressed patients with diffuse ground-glass opacities on CT after exclusion of competing diagnoses. Adjunctive corticosteroids are recommended for PCP with severe hypoxemia (PaO₂ <70 mmHg) despite limited evidence in non-HIV patients. CONCLUSION: We provide practical, resource-adapted guidance for managing fungal pneumonia in non-neutropenic ICU patients, while highlighting research priorities. The proposed diagnostic criteria for IPA and PM are provisional consensus-based frameworks intended to support clinical decision-making and require prospective multicentre validation. abstract: BACKGROUND: Tooth decay is a common problem, particularly among young patients. After incubation, biofilms were detached using saponin, serially diluted and plated on selective media, after which colony-forming units (CFU/mL and CFU/cm2) were calculated. The experiments were performed in 6 replicates using both static and dynamic (flow reactor) biofilm models. Cytotoxicity was evaluated according to the ISO 10993 standard using L929 fibroblasts and BALB/3T3 cells exposed for 24 h to extracts or disks containing Ag0 and CuO at concentrations of 0.125 wt%, 0.25 wt% and 0.5 wt%. RESULTS: Both Ag0 and CuO exhibited statistically significant dose-dependent antibacterial activity against S. mutans and S. epidermidis. Silver nanoparticles at concentrations of 0.25 wt% and 0.5 wt% demonstrated the highest cytotoxicity in both BALB/3T3 and L929 cell lines. CONCLUSIONS: The incorporation of both CuO and Ag0 particles into compomer materials enhanced their antimicrobial activity against S. mutans and S. epidermidis.
